# Eluned Parry

Archivist at the [[merrin-maritime-collection]]. Runs the reading room, the lifeboat station records and the fishing registers. The person who settled the lifeboat question.

## How we work together

- Book a reading-room day by email at least a week ahead, list the items wanted, and she pulls them. She prefers item references from the finding aid ([[merrin-lifeboat-station-records-finding-aid]]) to descriptions.
- On the [[merrin-archive-visit-2026-05-12|visit of 12 May 2026]] she brought out the station service records for three small stations and showed me that they were still launching pulling and sailing boats in the late 1920s, with motor boats arriving station by station as funds allowed. She also found a district inspector's letter recommending a motor boat for one station "when funds permit", which became the promised 1928 boat in the novel. See [[would-saltmarrows-lifeboat-have-had-an-engine-in-1927]].
- Followed up by email on 2026-05-15 with the references and two corrections to my notes ([[eluned-parry-email-2026-05-15]]).

## Current threads

- Whether the district committee minutes for 1928 survive; asked in October 2026, no answer yet.
- She would like to read the storm chapters before delivery. I have promised them once part two of the third draft is rewritten.

## Boundaries

Professional contact through the archive. She is careful to say what the records show and what they do not; my notes keep that distinction. Thanked in the acknowledgements, with her agreement.
